neighbours.label: 'seeing' / 'see' someone in the romantic sense (dating, an affair)
fire: Her parents were shocked to learn she had been seeing a married man.
After the breakup, Tom started seeing a nurse he met at the hospital.
They kept seeing each other in secret for almost two years.
He confessed that he was still seeing his ex-girlfriend on weekends.
Rumours spread that the senator was seeing one of his young aides.
We had only been seeing each other for a month when he proposed.
Is your sister still seeing that guitarist from the band?
Everyone at the office knew the manager was seeing the receptionist.
quiet: Her parents were shocked to learn she had been seeing double after the fall.
After the surgery, Tom started seeing colours more clearly than before.
They kept seeing deer in the garden for almost two years.
He confessed that he was still seeing spots in front of his eyes.
Rumours spread that the senator was seeing a specialist about his hearing.
We had only been seeing the coastline for an hour when the fog rolled in.
Is your sister still seeing the optician about her new glasses?
Everyone at the office was seeing the same error on their screens.

notes: Card: top peaks are ' seeing' in 'started seeing each other', 'been seeing someone else', plus 'dating', 'boyfriend' and custody 'visitation'. Near misses use 'seeing'/'see' in its literal visual sense in the same family settings, which tests the meaning against the word.
